evidence.text: The Commons file page identifies 八-oracle.svg as a digitally created vector redraw of a Shang oracle-script form. It names the Academia Sinica Sinica Database and gives a specific specimen reference: Xiaoxuetang glyph 41.E393, specimen 前2.32.4 / 合37459. It states CC0 1.0 for the file and the cited Sinica picture. The glyph is a modern redraw, not an oracle-bone photograph.
evidence.title: File:八-oracle.svg

evidence.text: The linked Academia Sinica page labels the glyph 甲骨文 and identifies it as 前2.32.4, 合37459, alongside the modern character 八. This supports the specimen provenance stated on Commons; the page presents a glyph record, not a photograph of the inscribed object.
evidence.title: 小學堂字形

evidence.text: The Commons file page identifies 八-bronze-warring.svg as a digitally created vector redraw in Warring States bronze-script style. It cites available paleographic databases and a bronze vessel reference, 丙辰方壺 西清19·3, and releases the representation into the public domain. It is a modern redraw, not a photograph of the bronze artifact.
evidence.title: File:八-bronze-warring.svg

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: cataloged historical script examples and formation analyses
evidence.text: The entry presents cataloged small-seal, bronze, oracle-bone and manuscript forms, and reports several competing analyses: diverging strokes for separation in the Shuowen tradition; concrete gesture/object proposals; 八 as an early graph for 分; and a proposal that its initial sense was 別. The entry also records oracle-bone numeral examples, including 八犬、八羊 in 合集 371正 and 八月 in 合集 6, with later bronze and Warring States manuscript numeral uses. It does not settle the competing graphic origins.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

search_audit.query: Wikimedia Commons 八 oracle bone script character file
search_audit.outcome: Found and opened two relevant Commons file pages. Both specify the historical script style, sources and reuse status; their original SVG URLs were exposed on-page but the web tool did not fetch image bytes.

search_audit.query: Wikimedia Commons 八 bronze script Chinese character glyph
search_audit.outcome: Opened the Warring States bronze redraw page. It cites the bronze vessel 丙辰方壺 西清19·3 and public-domain status.

search_audit.query: 八 甲骨文 字形 图片 Wikimedia Commons
search_audit.outcome: Opened the Commons candidate and the Academia Sinica linked glyph record. Direct image fetch failed with cache miss; source page identifies the specimen as 前2.32.4 / 合37459.
Opened Academia Sinica's 八 evolution record listing oracle bone, bronze, Chu manuscript and small-seal script categories, plus its traditional separation/borrowing interpretation.

gaps: The submitted candidates are digitally redrawn glyphs based on cataloged examples, not photographs of ancient artifacts. The visual agent must inspect the actual pixels before final selection.

The direct SVG file requests returned cache-miss or unsupported-content errors in the browsing tool; the opened Commons description pages establish candidate identity and stated reuse rights, but the image pixels were not visually inspected.

The file pages and catalog descriptions support period/script attribution and the nominated source examples, but neither image alone resolves the disputed origin of 八 or proves that it originally depicted a particular object.

items.period: Shang dynasty oracle-bone script; the source record identifies specimen 前2.32.4 / 合37459
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of 八 in Shang oracle script, linked to Academia Sinica specimen 前2.32.4 / 合37459. Oracle-bone examples are cataloged in the period as numerals; the graph's proposed separation origin remains debated.
items.alt: Two diverging strokes redrawn as an oracle-script glyph for 八.
items.selection_reason: A usable early-form candidate with unusually specific specimen provenance and stated CC0 reuse. It illustrates the early graph without claiming that the strokes depict a confirmed object.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, as stated for the redraw and source picture on the Commons file page.

items.period: Warring States period bronze-script style; source cited as 丙辰方壺 西清19·3
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of 八 in Warring States bronze-script style, sourced by Commons to 丙辰方壺 西清19·3. It offers a later comparison with the Shang oracle-script redraw; it is not an artifact photograph.
items.alt: A two-stroke 八 glyph in Warring States bronze-script style, represented as a vector redraw.
items.selection_reason: A second sourced period example shows a later script tradition and has an explicit source-object citation and public-domain release.
items.rights: Public domain; the Commons page states that the modern vector representation is released for unrestricted reuse.

limitations.text: Both candidates are modern vector redrawings, not photographs. This researcher did not inspect their pixels; visual selection and any shape-specific caption claims require the separate visual review.

The oracle file is directly tied to an Academia Sinica glyph record; the Warring States file cites a vessel source and paleographic databases. These descriptions establish candidates and provenance, not independent confirmation of every historical interpretation attached to 八.
